independence_declaration: The overlap set was coded without reading any other screener's output. No file named screen_batch_A.json / screen_batch_C.json / screen_batch_D.json was opened, and no overlap-set paper was discussed with another screener before this file was written. The only project files read before coding were paper/screen_protocol.md, paper/screen_frame.json and paper/screen_sample.json.
access_ladder_note: Rungs attempted for every record, in the order given in screen_protocol.md sec.7: (1) PubMed Central / publisher OA - succeeded for 18 records (PMC full text via NCBI efetch db=pmc); (2) publisher site direct - attempted for all 13 closed records, every one returned HTTP 403 or a bot-block stub (Springer, Elsevier/ScienceDirect, Wiley, Oxford, IEEE, RSNA); (3) institutional subscription - this screener holds none; (4) repository / accepted manuscript / preprint - Unpaywall, OpenAlex, Crossref and the arXiv API were queried for all 13; exactly one usable copy was found and used (PMID 34003056, version-of-record PDF, CC BY-NC-ND, University of Copenhagen repository). Unpaywall/OpenAlex additionally claimed OA for PMIDs 37222638 (Wiley pdfdirect) and 40335658 (Utrecht DSpace); both returned HTTP 403 in practice, which is a concrete instance of the sec.10 warning that oa_status is an automated hint and not a finding. The arXiv API returned an empty body, as it did during protocol development; (5) interlibrary loan / author request - not initiated, so the 21-day clock has not started. Sci-Hub and equivalent sources were NOT used.
supplement_note: PMC supplementary-file downloads were blocked from this environment (both the OA package endpoint and the per-article /articles/instance/.../bin/ endpoint returned HTML error stubs). Four included papers have supplementary material that could not therefore be searched: PMIDs 38337016, 40768653, 34003056 and 40442294. Their negative P1 codes are evidenced over the full main text only; this is recorded in each record's searches_run field and those rows are flagged.

batch_level_tallies._warning: These are tallies for 36 of the 100 sampled records (21 unique + 15 shared). They are NOT the study estimate. Pooling across screeners, deduplication of the overlap set and the sec.3.1 extension rule all happen later. Wilson intervals are shown only to indicate the precision available at this batch size.
